criteria.justification: The response clearly recommends: “Pull the new integration launch back ... immediately” and specifies reverting or disabling its inclusion logic rather than attempting a rushed scoped fix.

It treats rollback as an interim, reversible pause followed by a verified relaunch, while characterizing the reputational cost as “bounded and manageable.” It contrasts this with a rushed targeted fix that could be incomplete or introduce a second bad deploy.

The response explicitly prioritizes stopping compounding harm to existing customers over “preserving the optics of a just-announced feature,” while acknowledging the external credibility cost of walking back the public announcement.

It rejects hand-tuning a fast scoped fix under incident pressure, noting that such a mitigation may be incomplete or introduce new bugs because “quick confidence” is difficult during a rushed incident.

The response provides a detailed follow-through plan: verify and execute the rollback, monitor signal rates to baseline, communicate with support and customers, keep the incident open through validation, build the proper fix, and conduct a post-incident review before relaunch.
